statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk sits in the low band with orderly, two-sided overnight conditions.
recommendation: Conditions are described as orderly. The narrow danger window covering the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open and the 13:45 UTC flash PMIs is the main scheduled checkpoint; Tail remains below the block threshold on current evidence.
headline: Record Nasdaq close near session highs, quiet Globex tape, Tail stays low
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,732.40, up 0.82%, inside a 30,496.43-30,770.63 day range and near its high, alongside a second consecutive record Nasdaq Composite close driven by the AI-leadership bid. Globex NQ is trading around 31,052, roughly 0.1% higher, inside a narrow overnight range of about 70 points, so no persistent one-way structure has been observed since the reopen. VIX at 14.21, down 4.4%, and a 2Y/10Y pair at 4.76%/4.96% describe an orderly repricing environment rather than a stress regime. WTI slipped under $90 for a sixth straight session and Brent traded near $99 after Iran signalled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline; that de-escalation track lowers near-term energy pressure but leaves an unscheduled headline gap as the principal discontinuity risk. Mean reversion therefore appears available: retracement depth has been adequate, the index is not extending after failed pullbacks, and cross-asset signals are supportive rather than aligned into a single directional impulse. The clearest conditional risk is concentrated in the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMI release, where an opening-auction continuation leg would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held between 11 and 13 through the overnight and European sessions in a normal mode, lifted to 20-21 around the U.S. cash open and again into the 18:00-19:00 UTC power-hour window as trend-up structure developed, then decayed steadily to 14 by the 23:00 UTC hour as the record close settled and volatility drained. Stress peaked near 46 at the open and eased to the high 30s; Confidence stayed in the high band throughout, between 84 and 88.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are expected to stay in the low Tail band through the Asian and European sessions, with conditional risk concentrated in the 13:00-15:00 UTC block where the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs coincide. Two forecast hours reach the WATCH band on the possibility of an opening-auction continuation leg that denies early retracement; both decay quickly if price discovery is orderly. A modest power-hour uptick reflects late-session continuation risk into a potential record close. The main unscheduled risk remains an Iran/Strait of Hormuz headline discontinuity, which would raise Stress first and Tail only once a no-retracement path were actually observed.
